propositions: Long-running gate operations (close, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no output to stdout/stderr during execution, causing supervisor stall watchdogs to incorrectly kill healthy processes after 600 seconds of silence
Gate operations are the required final step for autonomous agent workflow completion; killing them leaves epic and story state stranded in progress with significant invested work at risk

Two dominant silent phases are local compute (27s prologue, 40s overlap retrieval) with no instrumentation at any log level, not model-call latency; raising REBAR_LOG_LEVEL reveals per-call lines but not these gaps

No total-runtime timeout exists in the gate path; time-to-first-token can legitimately be minutes per ADR 0089, but neither that ADR nor documentation justify the full silence duration or warn operators of supervisor budget interactions
Existing tests (test_llm_timeouts.py) affirmatively pin silence-tolerance as correct behavior, constraining any progress-emission remedy to be purely additive without introducing a total-runtime cap
